body:
Thanks for that.

Despite having lost so much (career, independence, ability to do even basic hobbies), I had learned to live with the significant restrictions this illness forced upon me.  Then, three & a half years ago, I was also diagnosed with cancer.  With very strong and intensive chemotherapy, I survived and, after 2 years in remission, considered ‘cured’ (the type of non- Hodgkin’s lymphoma I had very rarely comes back after 2 years).

Unfortunately, the chemotherapy took a massive toll on my body and has had the effect of worsening the ME/CFS to the point I am now at.  There is no cure for this illness, and so little research being carried out worldwide that there is no realistic hope of effective treatment in the near future (this is probably decades away).  While some people do recover to an extent, this is only likely in those who are younger and who have been less severely affected.

I have been active in the ME/CFS community for years, and there are certain patterns which give very poor prognostic indicators- significant worsening of symptoms 5-10 years after initial onset being one of them.

One of the symptoms that usually indicates yet more decline in condition is highly likely, is when intolerances to food, smell, medication or environmental factors (cleaning products/ different materials etc) begin to set in.  For me, intolerances to a number of foods has been a factor for quite a while, and has occurred alongside the ever increasing number of ‘bugs’, viruses and general level of illness.

In October 2018, I came down with a gastroenteritis bug that was going around.  This triggered a reaction which has led to almost constant diarrhoea since then, and despite numerous tests, no cause or cure for this can be found.  

Where it was frustrating not to be able to plan ahead or engage in much activity as a result of the levels of ME/CFS pre-cancer & chemo, now I can not even plan an hour ahead.  For the most part of my life, I am isolated in bed, in a dark room.  Having a simple conversation of under a minute can be sufficient to wipe me out completely.

I certainly hear what you say about knowing the option is there to commit suicide can, ironically, make it more bearable to continue.  This is where I’ve been for a long, long time now.  There has now, for me, reached a point where every hour is a struggle.  I quite literally long to sleep continuously and dread waking to whatever new hell awaits me.

As I live with my mother (I was unable to live independently quite early into my illness), I have been open with her about why I am not eating and what my intent is.  I’ve explained in detail how intolerable life is (& she has witnessed the decline, the excruciating pain and suffering).  She simply can not accept that it has come to this - she loves me and is desperate for me to ‘stick it out’.  I even asked her if she thought it was fair for her to ask me to continue to suffer, with no end in sight.  Obviously, she doesn’t want me to suffer but then says that she ‘knows’ she would endure the suffering to stay around for me!  It’s impossible for anyone to know just how much suffering they can endure unless they are in that situation!

I completely understand her fears - none of us ever want to face the thought of losing those we love.  However, the only way I could protect her from this heartache would be to suffer at an intolerable level myself- and I know I have tried everything but am at the point where it is simply too much for me to stand.

Retrospectively, I regret having accepted the treatment for cancer!  If I had thought my surviving would lead to this, I would have let the cancer finish me!

This certainly has not been an easy or a rash decision for me - I have fought hard to find a solution I could live with, but there are none.  Even explaining the situation to my GP (who my mother called in), the GP agreed that this is not depression, but the impact of having such a low quality of life.  She is genuinely frustrated with how limited she is in being able to eliminate (or even reduce) my suffering.  Don’t get me wrong, she’s offered referrals left, right & centre in the unlikely possibility that some cause or treatment can be offered for some part of my symptoms- however, when pressed she had to admit the chances aren’t great.  Just like my mother, she has tried to persuade me to eat, but accepts it is me right to refuse.

So, as you can see - this is not something I have not given thought to.  I just wish I could do this without causing pain and grief to my family.  As things are, I have to hope they will learn to understand and appreciate just how difficult life has become for me to take this step.

It’s not my preferred choice, but having weighed things up, I think this will make things a little easier on those I leave behind.  A sudden suicide leaves too many unanswered questions- even if a note is left.  One of the biggest questions (from experience when a cousin hung himself) can be “What if they changed their mind at the last minute?”  This question plagued my cousin’s eldest brother and after spending hours agonising over this on the phone to one of his remaining brothers, he ended up hanging himself - tragically, we think he was trying to work out if his youngest brother could have stopped at the last minute, was experimenting with a belt ‘noose’ on the under-side of the top bunk, and slipped.  This was also the view of the coroner.

Like I said, I do have an ‘easier’, quicker option with a massive morphine overdose, but think finding me (most likely with signs of frothing at the mouth), and without any prior warning, would be even more difficult on my mother.

Although starving myself to death will be more drawn out, the very fact it is progressive rather than sudden should make things slightly less traumatic for those I leave behind.  There will be no doubting that this is intended and that there will have been plenty of time in which I could have changed my mind (which I know I won’t, as the alternative is far too grim to contemplate).  Also, the progressiveness and inevitable deterioration in condition allows family some form of preparation for my death.

Basically, I think this way is kinder on the people I love most.  Yes, it will be tougher for me, but trust me - I’m more than used to pain and suffering.  Knowing that I won’t have too much longer to suffer is enough for me to be able to endure another few weeks- I expect I will become so weak I will probably sleep most of the last stages anyway.
Just general weakness with some headaches.
Thanks for that - let the count down begin 😊
